root_idea.summary: The root centers on firstness and beginning: the first part of the day, what comes first, and what is newly or initially produced.
root_idea.development: From the beginning of the day come meanings of going early and hastening; from firstness develop meanings of youth, virginity, first birth, first yield, and other figurative applications. A separate extension names the pulley and related ring forms.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Normalized as the verbal noun إِبْكَار, meaning early morning.
Displayed under the normalized citation form بِكْر, which covers its Quranic adjective and noun uses.
Displayed as the temporal noun بُكْرَة.
The QAC T grouping is the same lexical بُكْرَة and differs only grammatically in its temporal-adverbial use.

senses.definition: Early morning; the beginning of the day.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal-noun expression for entering or being in the early part of the day.

senses.definition: Young; in the Quranic description of the cow, not yet having borne offspring.
senses.usage_conditions: In 2:68 this describes a cow in contrast with an old cow; the broader lexical idea is youth or an early reproductive state.
The term can apply to a male or female; its Quranic plural أبكارًا is used of women who are virgins.

senses.definition: Early morning; the first part of the day.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a temporal noun and adverbially for the early part of a particular day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or apply oneself promptly to a need, task, destination, water, or meal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Originally associated with going early in the day, and also extended to hastening at any time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do, attend, or perform something at its earliest time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of going to prayer or performing prayer at the beginning of its appointed time; also of a palm tree that bears early.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To precede, go before, or take precedence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended use of the idea of being early or first.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone precede others or take precedence over them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative construction with a person or group as the object of precedence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have camels come to water early in the morning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive use concerning the timing of a herd’s arrival at water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause another to go or come early, or to cause another to hasten to an undertaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive counterpart of going early or hastening; the action may be understood temporally or as prompt application to a task.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To arrive early for the Friday prayer, especially in time for the opening portion of the sermon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression concerning early attendance at the mosque and the beginning of the Friday service.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or obtain the first portion of something, especially the first fruit to reach maturity; to eat the earliest ripe fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a first yield or first mature portion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a girl’s virginity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive use; one report further describes the act as occurring before puberty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To use or take fresh dough for preparing bread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage referring to dough newly prepared for use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a woman to bear her first offspring, in some usage specifically a male at her first birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive or prepositional construction concerning first childbirth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A youthful male camel or young camel in an early age category; figuratively, a young man or young woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Authorities differ over the precise camel-age range denoted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unpierced, unused, or not previously employed: specifically an unpierced pearl, a bow used for the first time, an unkindled fire, or a rain cloud likened to a virgin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are figurative or extended applications of untouched or first-use status.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female in a first reproductive state: one not yet having borne offspring, or, of a woman or she-camel, one that has borne only once.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source explicitly applies the term to women, cows or heifers, and she-camels in these reproductive conditions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grapevine that has produced fruit for the first time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of first production to a vine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Young offspring, especially young children or young bees; also honey associated with young bees or, in one usage, virgin girls.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural and collective applications extend the idea of youth or virginity to offspring and their products.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first-born child or offspring of a mother and father, whether male or female; also the first-born of animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may be applied beyond human offspring, including camels and other animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first of something, a first occurrence, or an action not previously preceded by its like.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can describe a matter being referred for the first time or a newly undertaken need or task.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A blow or stroke that kills or succeeds at once without requiring a second strike.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression for an immediately decisive action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sheave or pulley: a round piece with a rope-groove and a central axle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can refer to the sheave itself or, by synecdoche, to a complete pulley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small ring or bead-like ring attached to the ornamental part of a sword or scabbard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually occurring in the plural for the set of ornamental rings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An assembly, company, or congregated body; collectively, all together without anyone remaining behind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression جَاؤُوا عَلَى بَكْرَةِ أَبِيهِمْ is an idiom for coming together or in complete succession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain or a cloud that comes early in its season, at the end of the night, or at the beginning of the day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive adjective for rain or clouds that arrive early.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Early-producing or early-maturing; something that reaches fruit, growth, or maturity before others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to palm trees, fruit, land that produces vegetation quickly, and fruit that ripens first.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Winds that announce coming rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural figurative extension associated with signs that arrive before the rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The colors appearing on palm trees when their fruit begins to ripen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural term for early signs of the fruit’s ripening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Virginity or maidenhead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun referring specifically to a woman’s virginity in the cited definitions.

cautions: بِكْر has distinct Quranic branches: youth or an early reproductive state in 2:68, and virginity in أَبْكَارًا in 56:36 and 66:5.
Classical sources report variant age specifications for بَكْر when applied to camels; the entry therefore states the shared youthful meaning without fixing one age range.
